title: Trial deployment taktboard and resource emergency plan
content:
Context:
This is a working taktboard-style run diary for the Acme POC (trial deployment). The goal: validate latency and cost profile for the customer search-assistant workload under realistic traffic and demonstrate rollback + dedicated fallback within SLA windows. Focus areas: cold-start latency, multi-model routing, and prefix caching effectiveness.

Why taktboard?
- Provides a cadence-driven view: daily windows (takt) for measurable outcomes and resource handoffs.
- Useful for cross-team resource swaps (SRE, infra, SE) during short ramp periods.

High-level timeline (6 weeks):
- Week 0 (prep): infra provision + model pick + test prompts assembled (owners: Aisha, Owen)
- Week 1 (day-by-day): baseline smoke, A/B config, generate golden trace (owner: Meera)
- Week 2: traffic ramp to 25% production-sim, measure batching & KV cache hit rate (owner: Daniel)
- Week 3: full-lift stress days (2 nonconsecutive days), validate fallbacks and cross-region routing (SRE lead)
- Week 4: performance-tuning iteration, quantization profile tests (research)
- Week 5: customer-facing demo + runbook handoff, capture run metrics and checklist signoff

Daily takt windows (example for Week 2):
- 09:00-09:30: Standup + yesterday metrics (latency p50/p95/p99, token cost)
- 10:00-12:00: Controlled load test (25% sim), capture traces to /tmp/trial-traces/
- 13:00-14:00: Analysis + quick config adjustments (batching window size, LRU cache size)
- 15:00-17:00: Customer shadow traffic + session recording (consent pre-req)
- 17:30-18:00: End-of-day wrap: update taktboard, callouts to SRE if any incident

Acceptance criteria (minimal):
- p95 latency under 450ms on recommended model variant for 75% of tests
- Cost per 1k tokens within 10% of modeled estimate after batching and caching
- Seamless fallback: when primary pool exhausted, alternative model serves without >200ms extra latency
- E2E demo script runs without manual operator steps (automation checklist green)

Task tracker snapshot (working):
- TASK-001: provision dedicated pool (NVIDIA A10x) - owner: Owen - status: in_progress - notes: waiting on cloud quota increase request (ENG-2471)
- TASK-002: assemble golden prompt set (100 queries) - owner: Meera - status: done - notes: added edge-cases from customer corpus
- TASK-003: baseline latency run and trace capture - owner: Aisha - status: todo
- TASK-004: function-calling demo flow script - owner: Daniel - status: in_progress - notes: stubbed webhooks, need secret rotation step
- TASK-005: quantization smoke (8-bit) - owner: Research - status: blocked - notes: pending kernel compatibility patch in PR #789

Resource emergency plan (short form):
- Trigger conditions: sustained p95 > 900ms for 15 minutes OR error rate > 5% OR cache miss surge > 3x baseline.
- Immediate actions (first 15 minutes):
  1) Toggle conservative routing (route to dedicated fallback pool) - SRE or on-call (Daniel)
  2) Scale up burst capacity + enable burst GPUs (owner: Owen)
  3) Flip verbose logs for affected route and create retention snapshot for debug (Meera)
- If unresolved in 60 minutes:
  1) Fail open to lower-cost model maintained for latency (pre-approved by customer)
  2) Notify CS + customer point-of-contact with templated incident note
  3) Engage infra on emergency node replacement (escalate to infra manager)

Cross-team contacts (primary):
- Solutions Eng: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.ai)
- SRE on-call: Daniel Park (pager: SRE-rotation)
- Infra quota/limits: Owen Kim (slack: @owen-k)
- Research/quant: Meera Shah

Standup notes template (use daily):
- Yesterday: wins / blockers / anomalies (one-liners)
- Today: planned takt windows and owners
- Escalations: immediate actions and who owns them
- Metrics snapshot: p50/p95/p99, cache hit%, cost estimate delta

Decision ledger (living):
- 2025-11-05: Decided to use model-v2-compact for baseline due to quantization maturity (owner: Meera)
- 2025-11-12: Agreed to keep canary traffic at 25% for one full week before 50% ramp (owner: Aisha)

Open questions / research spikes:
- Is the customer's session churn causing KV cache fragmentation? (spike to measure session affinity)
- Can we shorten cold-start by pre-warming KV cache at 05:00 UTC? (runbook test)
- Quantization: does 4-bit int path preserve answer quality for low-temperature prompts? (eval set needed)

Notes to self / working hypotheses:
- Batching window of 10ms looked promising in dev but may increase tail latencies under burst; instrument with latency-per-batch-size metric.
- If dedicated pool shows >30% idle time during shadow runs, consider turning on multi-tenant bursts to sellback for internal workloads.

Next steps (this doc's immediate TODOs):
- [ ] Owen: follow up on cloud quota ticket and mark TASK-001 unblocked (due: 2025-11-06)
- [ ] Meera: upload eval set for quantization to linked artifacts and tag PR #789 for patch review (due: 2025-11-07)
- [ ] Aisha: schedule customer demo slot for Week 5 and draft demo runbook (due: 2025-11-10)

End of file. Save iterative notes here — this is intentionally informal. Keep taktboard updated daily and move items to Jira for permanent tracking.
